defs.en: Away from the surface of the Earth or other planet; in opposite direction to the downward pull of gravity.
defs.ex: I looked up and saw the airplane overhead.

defs.en: To or at a physically higher or more elevated position.
defs.ex: All day we climbed up and up.

defs.en: To an upright or erect position.
defs.ex: sit up; stand up; get up out of bed

defs.en: To a higher level of some quantity or notional quantity, such as price, volume, pitch, happiness, etc.
defs.ex: Gold has gone up with the uncertainty in the world markets.

defs.en: To or towards what is considered the top of something, irrespective of whether this is presently physically higher.
defs.ex: Go back up to the top of the page.

defs.en: Toward the top of.
defs.ex: The cat climbed up the tree.

defs.en: Toward the center, source, or main point of reference; toward the end at which something is attached.
defs.ex: The information made its way up the chain of command to the general.

defs.en: From south to north of.
defs.ex: We sailed up the East Coast of England from Ipswich to South Shields.

defs.en: Further along (in any direction).
defs.ex: Go up the street until you see the sign.

defs.en: From the mouth towards the source of (a river or waterway).
defs.ex: He led an expedition up the Amazon.

defs.en: Facing upwards.
defs.ex: Turn the cloth over so that the patterned side is up.

defs.en: On or at a physically higher level.
defs.ex: The flood waters are up again across large areas of the country.

defs.en: Headed or designated to go upward (as an escalator, stairway, elevator etc.) or toward (as a run-up).
defs.ex: Where is the up escalator?

defs.en: Fitted or fixed at a high or relatively high position, especially on a wall or ceiling.
defs.ex: All the notices are up now.

defs.en: Available to view or use; made public; posted.
defs.ex: Is your new video up yet? I looked on the website, but I couldn't find it.

defs.en: The direction opposed to the pull of gravity.
defs.ex: Up is a good way to go.

defs.en: A positive thing, or a time or situation when things are going well.
defs.ex: I hate almost everything about my job. The only up is that it's so close to home.

defs.en: An up quark.
An upstairs room of a two story house.
defs.ex: She lives in a two-up two-down.

defs.en: To physically raise or lift.
defs.ex: We upped anchor and sailed away.

defs.en: To increase the level or amount of.
defs.ex: If we up the volume, we may be able to hear what he says.

defs.en: To promote.
defs.ex: It wasn’t long before they upped him to Vice President.

defs.en: To rise to a standing position; hence, by extension, to act suddenly; see also up and.
defs.ex: She was sitting there quietly, then all of a sudden she upped and left.

defs.en: To upload.
defs.ex: 100 new apps and games have just been upped.

ja: 増やす、（値段など）引き上げる。

defs.en: Me and at least one other person, excluding the person(s) being addressed. (exclusive us.)
defs.ex: Don't treat us like idiots.

defs.en: Me and at least one other person, including the person(s) being addressed. (inclusive us.)
defs.ex: Let's ask him if he'll give us a lift.

defs.en: We, used in the same circumstances where “me” would be used instead of “I”, e.g. for the pronoun in isolation or as the complement of the copula
defs.ex: Who's there? — Us. (or) — It's us.

defs.en: Any entity that the speaker is a part of or identifies with, such as place of employment or education, nation, region, language, etc.
defs.ex: It's not true that the rest of Europe hates us.

defs.en: People in general.
defs.ex: Grief ages us.

ja: （第一人称複数目的格）私たちを（に）。
（第一人称複数主格）私たちが（は）。

defs.en: Designates the speaker(s)/writer(s) as constituting or belonging to the stated category of people (objective case).
defs.ex: It's not good enough for us teachers.

defs.en: Designates the speaker(s)/writer(s) as constituting or belonging to the stated category of people (subjective case).
Our.
defs.ex: We'll have to throw us food out.

defs.en: The relationship between the speaker and some other unspecified person.
defs.ex: There is no us.

defs.en: The act of using.
defs.ex: The use of torture has been condemned by the United Nations.

defs.en: The act of consuming alcohol or narcotics.
Usefulness, utility, benefit; purpose, point.
defs.ex: Near-synonyms: meaning, meaningfulness

defs.en: A function; a purpose for which something may be employed.
defs.ex: This tool has many uses.

defs.en: Occasion or need to employ; necessity.
defs.ex: I have no further use for these textbooks, but we may have use for all these other things later.

defs.en: To employ; to apply; to utilize.
defs.ex: Use this knife to slice the bread.

defs.en: To expend; to consume by employing.
defs.ex: I used the money they allotted me.

defs.en: To exploit.
defs.ex: You never cared about me; you just used me!

defs.en: To consume (alcohol, drugs, etc), especially regularly.
defs.ex: He uses cocaine.

defs.en: To consume a previously specified substance, especially a drug to which one is addicted.
defs.ex: Richard began experimenting with cocaine last year; now he uses almost every day.

ja: （私利の為に）利用する。搾取する。

defs.en: In used to.

ja: よく～したものだ（今はやっていない）

defs.en: That is or has or have been used.
defs.ex: The ground was littered with used syringes left behind by drug abusers.

defs.en: That has or have previously been owned by someone else.
defs.ex: He bought a used car.

defs.en: In used to.

ja: （叙述形容詞:be used toの形で）～するのに慣れている。

defs.en: Beneath; below; at or to the bottom of, or the area covered or surmounted by.
defs.ex: We found some shade under a tree.

defs.en: Below the surface of.
From one side of to the other, passing beneath.
defs.ex: I crawled under the fence.

defs.en: Less than.
defs.ex: Interest rates are now under 1%.

defs.en: Subject to.
defs.ex: We were constantly under bombardment.

defs.en: In or to a lower or subordinate position, or a position beneath or below something, physically or figuratively.
defs.ex: pulled under by the currents

defs.en: So as to pass beneath something.
defs.ex: There's quite a gap, so you may be able to sneak under.

defs.en: Less than what is necessary to be adequate or suitable; insufficient.
defs.ex: The plants were underwatered.

defs.en: In or into an unconscious state.
defs.ex: It took the hypnotist several minutes to make his subject go under.

defs.en: Down to defeat, ruin, or death.
defs.ex: The COVID-19 epidemic and shutdown took some businesses under.

defs.en: Lower; beneath something.
defs.ex: This treatment protects the under portion of the car from rust.

defs.en: In a state of subordination, submission or defeat.
defs.ex: The army could not keep the people under.

defs.en: Under anesthesia, especially general anesthesia; sedated.
defs.ex: Ensure the patient is sufficiently under.

defs.en: Having a particular property that is low, especially so as to be insufficient or lacking in a particular respect.
defs.ex: This chicken is a bit under.

defs.en: The amount by which an actual total is less than the expected or required amount.
Something having a particular property that is low or too low.
defs.ex: I went fishing but caught nothing but unders.

defs.en: A bet that a particular sporting statistic, such as points scored in a game, will be below a certain stated value.
Up to the time of (something happening); pending.
defs.ex: If you can wait until after my meeting with her, we'll talk then.

defs.en: Up to (a certain place)
defs.ex: Keep walking until the second set of traffic lights, then turn left.

defs.en: Before (a time).
Up to the time that the foods or other things available to sell, or tasks which need to be completed, run out.
defs.ex: Bake sale on Saturday, 2pm until.

defs.en: Up to the time that (a condition becomes true).
defs.ex: Not until I got his email did I fully understand his disappointment.

defs.en: Before (a condition becoming true).
Joined into a single entity.
defs.ex: Near-synonyms: combined, integrated

defs.en: Involving the joint activity of multiple agents.
defs.ex: The two parties stood united against the proposal.

defs.en: use; utilization
An institution of higher education that provides facilities for teaching, research, and the conferral of academic degrees across undergraduate, graduate, and often professional levels.
defs.ex: She's studying mathematics at university.

defs.en: To know the meaning of; to parse or have parsed correctly; to comprehend.
defs.ex: Can you repeat what you just said? I didn't understand.

defs.en: To know the meaning of.
To be thoroughly familiar with; to be able to undertake properly.
defs.ex: The students understood the assignment.

defs.en: To comprehend a fact or principle; to regard or come to regard a belief as such.
defs.ex: I understand that company policy says I can't get a refund, but can you make an exception?

defs.en: To know the intent, motives or character of; (of events) to know the causes of or reasons for.
defs.ex: One day you say you love me, the next you ignore me—I don't understand you!

ja: （語句などを補って）解釈する。

defs.en: Uh-huh, I see; a way to acknowledge something said by the other speaker.

syn: pick up what someone is putting down

defs.en: Most of the time; less than always, but more than occasionally.
defs.ex: Except for one or two days a year, he usually walks to work.

defs.en: Under normal conditions.
Initialism of “you know”.
alternative to on in most, though not all, prepositional uses.
The name of the Latin script letter U/u.
A thing in the shape of the letter U.
The act of uniting or joining two or more things into one.
The state of being united or joined; a state of unity or harmony.
Something united, or made one; something formed by a combination or coalition of parts or members; a confederation; a consolidated body; a league.
A trade union; a workers' union.
An association of students at a university for social and/or political purposes; also in some cases a debating body.
To combine sets using the union operation.
Belonging to, represented by, or otherwise pertaining to a labour union.
defs.ex: Actors have to be union to get work here.

defs.en: federal.
defs.ex: The union government of India

defs.en: Except on a specified condition; if not.
defs.ex: I’m leaving unless I get a pay rise.

defs.en: If not; used with counterfactual conditionals.
Except if; used with hypothetical conditionals.
